meta.notes: LIVE (logged out, iPhone UA 390x844, headless Chromium, 2026-11-08, www.pinterest.com): home /, pin /pin/1125968640422478/, profile /pinterest/, board /pinterest/kitchen-gamechangers-under-50/, search /search/pins/?q=test. All selectors are data-test-id/role anchors; the page is a React app with hashed classes, none used. Counts: signup-popup-dialog 1 on pin, profile, board and search (0 on home, where the sign-up screen is the page itself and must stay); with the dialog hidden the gated pin grid is fully visible and scrollable, no scroll lock, and no second pop-up appeared after 25 s of scrolling a search feed. The dialog holds the backdrop (mobile-modal-mask-overlay), the card (mobile-signup-mask), 'Get Pinterest app', email and Google buttons, so one rule removes it all. home-promo-sections 3, home-bottom-signup 1, home-footer-links 1 on / only. pin-more-to-explore 1 and pin-more-like-this-button 2 on the pin; board-more-like-this 1 on the board; pin-comment-button 1 and pin-author-followers 1 on the pin; profile-follow-counts 1 on the profile. Cards in feeds are gated-pin-rep divs without links logged out, so they were not touched. NOT SEEN on the real pages logged out: promoted/sponsored pins, shopping modules, comment sections (the comments panel is login-gated, only the button is present), notification prompts, cookie banners (none in this region), AI features; no rule was written for them. A Google One Tap iframe card showed over the search page once while the sign-up pop-up was open; it was not seen again and is not targeted. Logged-in pages were not visited. The related-pins selector will also hide the real feed under a pin, by design of that option.
